data.title: A statue of Old Orgoň and an information panel on Orgoňova Kýčera
data.excerpt: On 1 September 2018 a three-metre wooden statue of Old Orgoň was ceremonially unveiled on Orgoňova Kýčera, one of the highest hills in the Javorníky mountains. A new information panel made by our Hradiská civic association was installed with it, carrying the legend of the last pagan priest in the Javorníky.

children.text: On Saturday 1 September 2018 our association took part in an event — the ceremonial unveiling of the wooden statue of Old Orgoň on Orgoňova Kýčera — one of the highest hills in the Javorníky mountains. It stands on the boundary between Dolná and Horná Mariková and a fine legend is linked to it, about the mysterious Orgoň — the last pagan priest in the Javorníky, who in the Middle Ages refused, right up to his mysterious end, to accept the new religion, Christianity, and remained faithful to the old pagan gods.

The statue is the work of the gifted woodcarver Vladimír Ragula from Hatné. The whole event was organised by the mayor of Horná Mariková, Mr Miroslav Hamár. Besides the unveiling of the three-metre statue, a new information panel was also installed on Kýčera, which carries the legend of Old Orgoň as retold by Štefan Meliš and Stanislav Muntág. The panel was created by our Hradiská civic association.

The event on Kýčera itself was superbly organised, for which thanks are due to the mayor of Horná Mariková. Chilled draught beer and excellent hunter’s goulash made the whole occasion more pleasant for the people who gathered here in truly large numbers. All that remains is to keep our fingers crossed for Old Orgoň, that he will guard Kýčera for the coming decades and will not fall victim either to the forces of nature or to ill-willed people.
